title: Which channels and content produce pipeline, Jan to Sep 2026

findings: Partner referrals are 6% of leads and 4% of spend (EUR 8k), but 45% of pipeline (EUR 2.84m), 50% of won deals and 66% of won revenue. That is EUR 355 of pipeline per EUR spent.
LinkedIn Ads takes 35% of spend (EUR 78k) and returns 9% of pipeline. Cost per SQL is EUR 4,333, the worst of any channel.
LI_AI_Delivery_Q2 spent EUR 41k for 151 leads and 109 MQLs, and produced zero SQLs and zero pipeline.
Case studies are 24% of first touches but 45% of SQLs and 45% of pipeline, with a 15% SQL rate. Blogs and the AI webinar bring 541 leads and 310 MQLs but only 16 SQLs (3%).

The MQL count rewards the wrong content: the AI webinar produces the most MQLs (118) and one of the lowest MQL to SQL rates. CTOs and VPs of Engineering convert to SQL at about 13%; developers and marketing managers at under 3%.
cleaning: Removed 12 exact duplicate rows (1,412 to 1,400). Lead IDs are unique after that.
Mapped 18 source spellings to 6 channels that match the spend file (e.g. 'linkedin ads', 'LinkedIn' and 'LinkedIn Ads' all become LinkedIn Ads).
Converted 204 dates from DD/MM/YYYY to ISO, and added a created_month column.
Converted 5 deal values stored as text (e.g. '€56,500') to numbers.
Standardised casing on 43 job titles and set 58 blank regions to 'Unknown'. Blank campaigns (organic, partner, events, outbound) are '(none)'.

Stage became cumulative 1/0 flags: is_mql (MQL or later), is_sql (SQL or later), is_opp (Opportunity, Closed Won or Closed Lost), is_won. Pipeline value is the deal value on every opportunity, open or closed; deal values only exist on those rows.
caveats: Channel and content are first touch only. A partner lead may have read three case studies first; this data cannot show that.
Won-deal counts are small outside partners (3 to 5 per channel), so revenue by channel is directional. Pipeline and SQLs are the more stable comparison.
September has 70 leads and EUR 88k pipeline. August and September leads have not had time to progress, so recent months understate.
Spend is a Jan to Sep total per channel, so efficiency cannot be tracked by month. Partner spend of EUR 8k may not include partner fees or staff time.
Pipeline per EUR for organic and partners depends on how complete their spend figures are.
next_steps: Pause LI_AI_Delivery_Q2 and GA_Outsourcing_Generic (EUR 75k combined, 5 SQLs) and move budget into the partner programme and case-study offers aimed at CTOs and VPs of Engineering.
Make the two case studies the default offer in LinkedIn retargeting and Google Brand, the two paid campaigns with the best pipeline per EUR.
Report on SQLs, pipeline and pipeline per EUR instead of MQLs, and add a multi-touch content field to the CRM so content gets credit beyond first touch.
